known.title: Decision 2 skips fenced code blocks on the false premise that a fence holds only example commands, so machine paths in fenced command output get no advice.
known.summary: Decision 2 now skips fenced code blocks with blankFencedRegions() because 'a fence holds example commands, not paths of this machine'. The premise is false: plan-contract.md at 3ac23ad8d45b485374ae33ae025f199bd8a34d27 records in Verification Results the 'Commands run, results' (line 49), `export` prints an 'Absolute path to plan-<n>.md in the scratch directory' (line 185), and scripts/AGENTS.md says a failed ci.mjs task prints the exact paths of its retained temporary spool (lines 86-89). Agents paste such output in fences, so a fence is the most likely place for a home, scratch, or temporary path. The current helper scans fences: the regex in plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs (lines 565-570) runs on the cleaned text with only link targets removed, and blankFencedRegions() (line 28) is used only for headings, tables, and Mode lines (lines 454, 492, 528, 674). A fenced `/home/<user>/src/app/.git/docks-review/plan-72.md` gets advice from the helper at 3ac23ad8d45b485374ae33ae025f199bd8a34d27 and from the landed fix. Effect: the change makes the advice miss the paths that 'Keep scratch and machine paths out of durable records' (plan-contract.md line 202) targets, so the Goal (line 6: flag a path that points into one machine) is not reached.

known.title: Decision 3 claims that test() and matchAll() on one module-level regex with the g flag keep no state between calls, but test() advances lastIndex and matchAll() starts from it.
known.summary: Decision 3 keeps the test() gate and collects the paths with matchAll() on the same module-level regex with the g flag, 'neither method keeps state between calls'. MDN RegExp.prototype.test() (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/RegExp/test): with the global flag, test() advances lastIndex, further calls resume from lastIndex, and lastIndex does not reset while test() returns true, 'even when testing a different string'. MDN RegExp.prototype[Symbol.matchAll]() (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/RegExp/Symbol.matchAll): 'lastIndex starts as the original regex's value'. ECMA-262 confirms both (https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/text-processing.html#sec-regexp-prototype-%25symbol.matchall%25 copies lastIndex into the matcher; #sec-regexpbuiltinexec reads lastIndex when the g flag is set). Effect: the gate moves lastIndex past the first path, so matchAll() never names it, and the state carries into the next normalizePlan() call; one command calls normalizePlan() several times (plan.mjs at 3ac23ad8d45b485374ae33ae025f199bd8a34d27 lines 574, 598-599, 665, 755-756, 811, 833, 849). A test-gated copy of the landed helper printed only the /home/<user>/x line for the A2 input, and for one body three calls gave [/home/<user>/x], [], [].

known.title: Acceptance A2 prints only the first advice line with find(), so it passes when the helper names only the first machine path or misses the home path.
known.locator: Acceptance, row A2 (line 46); Goal (line 7); Research, Decisions, decision 3 (line 28)
known.summary: A2 now uses advice.find(...) and expects only 'body contains an absolute machine path: /tmp/run-1'. Goal line 7 requires one advice line per distinct path, and decision 3 requires body order and the trailing '.' trim, but find() returns the first matching line only. A helper that names only the first match (the #71 proposal 'Print the first match'), that does not flag /home/<user>/x, or that keeps its trailing '.' still passes A2. A1 runs only the cases that the implementer writes, so no acceptance row checks the one-line-per-path goal. Checked: the seeded A2 command runs at 3ac23ad8d45b485374ae33ae025f199bd8a34d27 (prints the old fixed text); with the landed helper (ea39471) and with a copy that breaks after the first advice line, the seeded A2 prints the same /tmp/run-1 line for both, while the original A2 (filter and join, exactly two lines) fails the first-only copy.

known.title: Step 4 runs the release without an in-session ask because it treats the release as landing work that the settled Mode covers, which the contract forbids for a non-local Effect step.
known.summary: Step 4 (Effect release) says the settled plan-and-implement Mode covers this landing work, so the step needs no new ask. plan-contract.md at 3ac23ad8d45b485374ae33ae025f199bd8a34d27: 'Every non-local step requires an in-session ask immediately before it runs. Persisted Effect values record intent, not permission.' (lines 89-90), `release` is a non-local token (line 86), Mode covers routine issue publication and landing work 'which stay outside the Steps table' (lines 33-34), and a step after the landing merge runs only after 'ask in session' (lines 306-308). Root AGENTS.md line 79 and plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/SKILL.md lines 27-30 repeat the rule and keep the Mode coverage to routine issue publication and linked-branch landing work; the helper itself prints 'step <id> Effect release needs an in-session ask before it runs.' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs line 546). Effect: the release commit, tag push, and public GitHub release run without the permission that the contract requires.
